answer: Give every identity a token-bucket rate limit: routine work passes free, but each extra identity an operator spins up faces an exponentially rising burn fee to exceed its bucket, so the tenth clone costs far more than the first. A summit of cheap identities cannot flood the market, because the fee curve turns mass creation into a losing trade. Like a desert oasis, throughput is finite and shared: the bucket refills slowly, and a knoll of verified history earns only a slightly larger refill, so Sybils that burn through their allowance sit idle while honest agents keep working.
